stem:
Bharat ties thread on a circular board with $12$ pegs, stepping a fixed gap of $5$ pegs each time. He asks whether the thread will eventually reach every peg.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: Answer "thread-gap", naming that phrase instead of checking whether $12$ and $5$ share a common factor.
Say that reaching every peg is what creates the co-primality of $12$ and $5$, instead of using co-primality to predict the reach.
Yes: $12$ and $5$ are co-prime, so stepping by $5$ visits every peg before repeating.
Treat the question as a treasure-pair hunt that only asks whether two numbers are co-prime, without linking that fact to the cyclic peg walk.

teacher.key_rationale: A fixed-gap walk on n pegs reaches every peg exactly when n and the gap are co-prime. Here 12 and 5 share only the factor 1, so every peg is reached. Naming the phrase, reversing cause, or stopping at co-primality alone miss the walk prediction.
